prompt: A checkout request touches nine services and takes 4 seconds. Each team says their service is fast.
tells: Each team says their service is fast
why: A trace shows each hop's duration on one timeline, so you can see where the 4 seconds go.
trap: Per-service dashboards average over all requests and hide the slow path.

prompt: A customer's order was charged but never shipped. You need to follow that one request through the gateway, payments, queue and fulfillment.
why: Search by trace or request ID and follow it hop by hop to where it stopped.
trap: Grepping each service's logs separately, without a shared ID, rarely lines up.

prompt: A page sometimes takes 3 seconds. A timeline view of one slow request shows 200 tiny sequential calls to the same downstream service.
tells: timeline view of one slow request
why: The trace exposes an N+1 call pattern; batch the calls.
trap: No single call is slow, so per-endpoint metrics look healthy.

prompt: One user request becomes 27 calls to the database. You suspect each of three layers retries three times, but need to see it.
tells: each of three layers retries three times
why: A trace shows nested retries per layer; then retry at only one layer.
trap: It amplifies load like a retry storm, but first you need to see where retries happen.
